text: {"distance_m": 3.4, "reasoning_short": "The spot behaves as a small, low-contrast target, so detection rather than resolution sets the limit. Below roughly 6 arcmin, Ricco's law makes threshold contrast fall roughly with target area. My approximate recollection of Blackwell-type indoor data is that a dark disc about 0.6 arcmin across needs near-100% contrast. A 30% spot then needs about 0.6/sqrt(0.3), or roughly 1.1 arcmin, so about 1 arcmin. A 1 mm spot subtends 1 arcmin (0.00029 rad) at about 3.4 m. This is an estimate, not a precise threshold."}
